audit.why: Packet win rate is 60.0 over only 10 games. The stored EVEN / 5.5-10 framing is the honest read for a sample that small; no change proposed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on the level chart. content.win is [Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Skill] but full.phases sides are [Mel,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill].
audit.why: Pre-6 is genuinely Mel-sided (his only gap-close is a 365-range Jaws of the Beast lunge). From 6 on, Infinite Duress plus Flash is a real kill path, so Skill is right there. The correct shared chart is Mel/Mel/Mel/Mel/Skill/Skill/Skill.
audit.corrected: Set content.win[1..3] and full.phases[1..3].side to Mel; set content.win[4] and win[5] to Skill. NOT proposed as an edit because a side value swap (Mel<->Skill) cannot satisfy the +/-10% length band; flagged for the user to apply by hand.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text claims the first-item spike comes from reflecting Warwick's projectiles with Rebuttal.
audit.why: Warwick's kit contains no projectile. Eternal Hunger, Jaws of the Beast, Blood Hunt, Primal Howl and Infinite Duress are all non-projectile, so Rebuttal's reflect has literally nothing to send back. The real first-item lever is anti-heal.
audit.corrected: Rewrote the spike around Morellonomicon versus Eternal Hunger's sub-25% triple healing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (no projectile flag on any slot)

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup never names a single Warwick ability in the content layer and never states the decisive interaction: Solar Snare's root denies both of Warwick's movement abilities.
audit.why: Jaws of the Beast (Q) and Infinite Duress (R) are both dash-class movement abilities. A rooted champion cannot cast a dash, so a landed Solar Snare removes Warwick's entire approach and his entire engage for its duration. This is the single most useful fact in the matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Named all five abilities across both layers and made the root-denies-lunge-and-leap interaction the spine of the early game text.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (dash flag on Q and R)

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] says 'his passive heals hardest as you're low'.
audit.why: Eternal Hunger keys off WARWICK's health, not Mel's: it heals below 50% and the healing triples below 25%. The text inverts the mechanic, which teaches the player to chip him into his strongest sustain window and then wonder why he does not die.
audit.corrected: Rewrote to state Eternal Hunger triples when Warwick drops under 25%.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blood Hunt is never mentioned, and the 50% health trigger is never stated.
audit.why: Blood Hunt senses enemies below 50% health and grants Warwick move speed toward them, tripled under 25%. That threshold is the whole positioning rule for a 550-range immobile mage: above 50% he cannot catch her, below it he can. It also means a chipped Mel is visible to him across the map.
audit.corrected: Stated the 50%/25% thresholds in whys[2], wants.foe[0], phases[3].why and the late-game text.

audit.why: Primal Howl grants damage reduction for 2.5 seconds before the fear fires. Golden Eclipse is a single damage instance, so detonating it into an active Primal Howl throws away the whole stack payoff. Its cooldown is 15/14/13/12/11.
audit.corrected: Added the 2.5s damage-reduction warning to whys[4] and the real cooldown to breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.trading all say Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'. breakdown.cooldowns lists no real numbers at all.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26 seconds. At the rank you actually have in lane it is 38 seconds, nearly double what the text claims, which makes a bad trade sound recoverable when it is not. Infinite Duress is 110/90/70 and Primal Howl 15/14/13/12/11.
audit.corrected: Replaced 'twenty seconds' with the real 38s figure and put the true numbers into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization says 'add anti-heal early' without naming an item, and phases[5] implies Blackfire Torch handles his sustain.
audit.why: Blackfire Torch is a burn and damage-amp item; it applies no Grievous Wounds. Against a champion with healing on P, Q and R, the anti-heal has to be an actual Grievous Wounds source (Morellonomicon on an AP mage).
audit.corrected: Named Morellonomicon in phases[5].why and the itemization line instead of implying the Torch covers it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (heal flag on P, Q, R)

audit.whatIsWrong: Infinite Duress's leap distance is treated as fixed.
audit.why: The leap scales with Warwick's bonus move speed, so an active Blood Hunt turns a short engage into a screen-crossing one. A Mel player who has only ever seen the base range will stand at a distance she believes is safe.
audit.corrected: Stated the Blood-Hunt-scaled leap in spikes[3].text, wants.foe[1] and dosFull[0].d.

edits.after: Q poke plus Solar Snare's root lands a free punish on Warwick as he steps up for a creep — rooted, Jaws of the Beast cannot lunge.

edits.before: Warwick has no dash and only W move-speed to reach you, so the early game is yours to dictate from 550 range. At level 2 grab Q + E: when he steps up to last-hit, land Solar Snare's root and free-poke him with Q while he's stuck, stacking Overwhelm. Don't waste E as a panic button — it's your anti-engage tool, so hold it if he's hovering W to walk you down. His passive heals hardest when HE is low, not when you are, so keep him topped off on poke damage you take back, not the reverse.
edits.after: Jaws of the Beast lunges only 365 units, so the early game is yours to dictate from 550 range. At level 2 grab Q + E: when he steps up to last-hit, land Solar Snare's root — rooted he cannot lunge at all — and free-poke him with Q while he's stuck, stacking Overwhelm. Don't waste E as a panic button; it's your anti-engage tool, so hold it if he's hovering Blood Hunt to walk you down. Eternal Hunger heals him under 50% health and triples that healing under 25%, so never leave him parked in that window.

edits.before: This is your takeover. As Q ranks up you out-poke his Q-heal sustain — he can't drain what he can't reach. At 6, Golden Eclipse turns your accumulated Overwhelm stacks into burst from range; bait his W-walkup, root with E, then detonate R to chunk or execute. His one real threat is R suppress: it locks you in place and his low-HP passive heals him through your damage, so respect it off Flash and keep W ready to wall his engage. With first item you're at your most dominant — chain Q pokes freely.
edits.after: This is your takeover. As Q ranks up you out-poke Jaws of the Beast's healing — he can't drain what he can't reach. At 6, Golden Eclipse turns your accumulated Overwhelm stacks into burst from range; bait his walk-up, root with Solar Snare, then detonate to chunk or execute. His one real threat is Infinite Duress, 110 seconds at rank 1 — a whiffed one leaves him answerless for nearly two minutes. Buy Morellonomicon by your second item; his sustain is the matchup.

edits.before: You owned the lane, but late is where a fed-free Warwick claws back. Once he's itemized with a R Flash setup, a single suppress can delete your squishy frame before you cast — you have zero dashes and only E to peel. Never facecheck or sidelane alone where he can engage from fog; stay with your team, use W to wall his all-in and E to break his chase. Your infinitely-scaling passive keeps you relevant, but you win by closing the game on the lead you built, not by 1v1ing a drain tank with R up.
edits.after: You owned the lane, but late is where a farmed Warwick claws back. Infinite Duress is 70s at rank 3 and its leap scales with his Blood Hunt speed, so a single suppress can delete your squishy frame before you cast — you have zero dashes and only E to peel. Blood Hunt also senses anyone under 50% health, so never sidelane chipped: that is exactly how he picks his target. Stay with your team, hold W for the real all-in, and close the game on the lead you built rather than duelling a drain tank with R up.

notes: LEVEL CHART MISMATCH (needs a human): content.win for mel/warwick is [Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Skill] while full.phases sides are [Mel,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill]. The two layers show different charts for the same matchup. Correct shared chart is [Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Skill,Skill,Skill]. I did not propose it as an edit because swapping a side value between 'Mel' (3 chars) and 'Skill' (5 chars) cannot pass the +/-10% length band. KIT FLAG NOTE: mel.json flags W Rebuttal with 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'. Riot's own description for Rebuttal says only that it is a barrier that reflects projectiles, prevents damage and grants move speed — nothing about terrain. The existing copy leans on 'wall his engage' in several places; I left that wording where it already existed rather than amplify it, but whether Rebuttal physically blocks a path is unverified and should not be built on further. REFLECT IS DEAD HERE: Warwick has no projectile on any slot, so Rebuttal's reflect contributes nothing in this matchup — the old spikes[2] text was selling a mechanic that does not exist. SUSPECTNAMES ARE FALSE POSITIVES: the packet flags "E's Solar Snare" and "Solar Snare's" as probable wrong names; Solar Snare is Mel's real E, and both hits are just possessive forms.
